cases.description: A level-1 heading that is the first block and the record's only level-1 heading gives the root's $title, and the text under it is the root's $body.

A level-1 heading after a paragraph is not the first block, so the root has no $title and the heading starts a section. The root's $body as the text before the first heading rests on a reading of §5.3, which defines $body only after a heading.

The first block is a paragraph, so the root has no $title, and each level-1 heading is a section of the root; the case does not test the only-level-1-heading clause, whose input needs a root without text. The root's $body as the text before the first heading rests on a reading of §5.3, which defines $body only after a heading.
check warns about a record with several level-1 headings, at the root, and the record stays readable.
check does not warn about a record whose only level-1 heading is its title.

The title heading's anchor element gives the root's $anchor and $tags, and is not part of its $title; $tags as the class tokens in source order is a reading, since the draft states neither the order nor what a repeated token gives.
A # line inside a fenced code block is not a heading (CommonMark 0.31.2, 4.5), so the title heading is still the record's only level-1 heading.
A setext heading underlined with = is a level-1 heading (CommonMark 0.31.2, 4.3), so as the first block and the only one it gives the root's $title; one underlined with - starts a level-2 section.
